title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with behavior expected by downstream SDKs and customers. This PR aligns parameter handling (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty), message roles parsing, stop-token semantics, logprobs support, and structured/response-formatting outputs. It also stabilizes streaming behavior for tool/function calls and structured output to avoid truncated partial events seen in canary tests.

What this PR does:
- Adds full param mapping and validation for OpenAI-style fields at the gateway (max_tokens, n, stop, logprobs, echo, user).
- Normalizes message role handling (system/user/assistant) and accepts legacy 'bot' alias in requests to minimize client breakage.
- Implements stop token logic that supports list and string forms and matches OpenAI semantics (respecting tokenization boundaries where possible).
- Adds first-class logprobs support in the compatibility layer: forwards logprobs request to runtime when model/kernel supports it and falls back with clear error when not supported.
- Improves streaming stability for function/tool calls: ensures function call begin/finish events are emitted atomically and adds buffering logic to prevent split JSON fragments in SSE/chunked responses.
- Adds structured output post-processing to support response_formatting and schema-enforced outputs coming from RLHF/evaluation branches.
- Updates SDK compatibility testmatrix and adds new e2e tests that exercise roles/stop/logprobs/formatting across streaming and non-streaming paths.

Checklist:
- [x] API parameter mapping and validation
- [x] Role normalization and legacy alias support
- [x] Stop token handling for string/list inputs
- [x] Logprobs plumbing + graceful fallback
- [x] Streaming stability fixes for function/tool calls
- [x] Structured output formatting and schema enforcement
- [x] End-to-end tests + integration test updates
- [x] Docs update (openai compatibility page)

Testing notes: Ran redwood/serving unit and integration test suites. New e2e tests added (tests/e2e/openai_chat_parity/*) that run against canary runtime and a pinned model with logprobs enabled. Canaries initially exposed a flaky behavior where partial JSON for function calls would be emitted across two frames; buffering + backpressure fixes removed the flakiness in repeated runs. CI: a flaky streaming e2e job was re-run once and passed.

Backward compatibility: Non-breaking for most customers. We accept legacy role alias 'bot' and default older client semantics when 'compat:legacy' header is present. However, enabling logprobs may increase latency for models not optimized for returning token-level metadata; documented in release notes.

Notes for reviewers: Key files are small but critical; pay attention to OpenAI parameter edge cases in gateway mapping and the SSE buffer size tuning in streaming_io. The structured output post-processing is intentionally conservative; we coerce non-conforming outputs to an error when schema enforcement is requested.

review_comments: Owen Lancaster: Please ensure the stop-token logic respects multibyte token boundaries; tests should include UTF-8 edge cases.
Maya Chen: Added boundary tests for utf8/emoji cases and included a short note in docs about tokenization caveats.
Priya Patel: The streaming buffer default looks high (64KB) — can we make it dynamic based on content-type and streaming rate?
Maya Chen: Switched to dynamic sizing: baseline 8KB; auto-grow to 64KB for large function call payloads. Added config flag streaming.buffer.max_bytes.
Ravi Singh: Logprobs endpoint should return 400 with helpful message when requested on unsupported runtime rather than 500.
